_comment: THE TOE (docs/plan_early_game_labor.md 'Equipment / TOE', docs/plan_hunt_through_combat.md 4.8). TWO NOUNS, AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME: an ITEM is a piece of equipment (spears, sled, baskets, traps) that owns its own effects, its own durability and its own use quantum; a KIT is a roster entry that LISTS the items a party is sent out with. The items used to be named `hunting_kit`/`sled_kit`/`basket_kit`, which called both concepts 'kit' and made a kit look like a leaf; they are `items` now and 'kit' means only the roster entry. Consumable, START-STOCKED and NOT CRAFTABLE: running one dry is the intended pressure and the pull into the Milestone-2 crafting economy. TWO TIERS, NEVER A TAPER: performance is FLAT until expiry and then the role STEPS DOWN - durability and performance are deliberately ORTHOGONAL axes so a future crafting system can tune them independently. THE TIER IS PER-BAND, PER-ROLE, not per-hunter inventory. WEAR IS CHARGED FOR USE, NEVER FOR TURNS ELAPSED (docs/plan_denial_raid.md 1.2): a turn clock would charge an idle march the same as a slaughter, which would make denial free. QUALITY TIERS (flint vs bronze spears) are NOT here: they are unobtainable until something can craft them, so they ride the crafting slice. PLAYTEST DIALS.
_comment_effects: AN EFFECT NAMES THE VALUE A STAT TAKES, never a delta and never a multiplier stacking on something else - that is what keeps 'flat until expiry, then a step down' structurally true instead of a rule someone has to remember. Each effect declares exactly ONE tier, and WHICH tier it declares is the one-home-per-fact rule showing through: the OTHER tier already had a home and keeps it. `equipped` = the value while the item is intact, so the baseline lives elsewhere (attack's bare-handed 1.0 is creatures.json `person.combat.attack`; dispersion/engage_multiplier/exposure are all NEUTRAL AT 1.0, which is why an item that does not mention them changes nothing). `unequipped` = the value once the item is spent, so the equipped value lives elsewhere (the hunt's 40.0 is labor_config.json `hunt.per_worker_biomass_capacity`, the gather's 8.0 its `forage.per_worker_biomass_capacity` - the rates the shipped, start-kitted game has always run on). Copying either into this file would give a shipped number a second home to drift from.
_comment_shapes: THE TWO CARRY ITEMS WANT DIFFERENT SHAPES, NOT MERELY DIFFERENT NUMBERS (4.8). FORAGE IS CONTAINMENT-BOUND - bare hands is a handful against a basketful - so its ratio is LARGE: 8.0 equipped against 1.6 bare, exactly one fifth, which is about what a forager keeps when the only vessel is two cupped hands and the fold of a hide. THE HUNT IS TRANSPORT-BOUND - a sledless party can always drag SOMETHING - so its ratio is SMALLER: 40.0 equipped against 12.0, under a third. The hunt's shortfall needs no new mechanic: a party that cannot haul its kill leaves more of it on the range, which AnimalTake.wasted already computes and the client already shows.
_comment_declaring_the_neutral: SPEARS DECLARE `dispersion 1.0` AND `exposure 1.0` THOUGH BOTH ARE THE NEUTRAL VALUE, and that is load-bearing rather than noise. A kit resolves a multiplier stat as the MAXIMUM of what its LIVE items DECLARE, and an item that says nothing contributes nothing (not the neutral) - which is what stops the sled, carry gear nobody approaches an animal with, from dragging a trapping party's dispersion back to 1.0 just by being in the kit. The declaration is therefore what makes a spears-AND-traps kit resolve to LOUD and EXPOSED instead of inheriting the trap's stand-off for free: if you are running up throwing spears you are scaring the herd and you are in reach of it, however many traps you also set. Nothing shipped pairs them today; the declaration is what keeps the answer right the day something does.
_comment_dispersion: DISPERSION MULTIPLIES THE QUARRY'S OWN FLIGHT RESPONSE: effective_wariness = clamp(wariness * dispersion, 0, 1), and stayers = engaged * (1 - effective_wariness). It is NEUTRAL AT 1.0, so every item that does not declare it - and every kit that carries no item declaring it - leaves the shipped retreat untouched. TRAPS SHIP 0.0: a trap line does not scare anything, because nothing runs up to the animal. THE SPECIES DECIDES HOW MUCH IT MATTERS, which is the whole reason this is a multiplier and not a subtraction: a Gazelle at wariness 0.85 loses almost everything to a noisy approach while a Mammoth at 0.10 barely notices, so ONE spear line scatters a warren and contains a mammoth with no special-casing and no per-target authoring. wariness 0 is already an exact identity in the retreat (no draw is made), so dispersion 0 lands in a regime the sim has always had rather than a new one.
_comment_exposure: EXPOSURE IS WHETHER THE ITEM'S USERS ARE IN REACH OF THE ANIMAL, and it multiplies the hunt's baseline injury hazard (fauna::hunt_injuries = combat_config.hunt_injury_damage_per_animal * animals engaged * lethality). NEUTRAL AT 1.0. TRAPS SHIP 0.0 - a trap is a stand-off instrument, so it wears out INSTEAD of the trapper getting hurt, which is the trade and not a free lunch. It is deliberately NOT a weapon-vs-gear classification: what matters is whether the users are exposed, because that is what the resolver keys casualties on.
_comment_durability: DURABILITY IS A 0-100 CONDITION SCALE ON EVERY ITEM, and the per-use wear rate is what says how long each lasts - that is what keeps the two axes orthogonal (change how long an item lasts without touching what it does). A band carries WEAR (BandEquipment, persisted); an item is EQUIPPED while its wear is strictly below its starting_durability, and the drop at expiry is a cliff. Spears: 100 / 0.4 per kill = 250 kills. Sled: 100 / 0.02 per biomass hauled = 5000 biomass. Baskets: 100 / 0.04 per biomass gathered = 2500 biomass. Traps: 100 / 0.2 per kill = 500 kills, twice the spear's life per kill because a trap is worked rather than thrown - and it is charged on the SAME quantum as spears so a trapping party cannot hunt for free. AGAINST THE SHIPPED ~16-WORKER STARTING BAND THE BASKET HITS plan_early_game_labor's ~15-20 TURN KIT-DURATION TARGET AND THE TWO HUNT ITEMS OVERSHOOT IT BY ~3x (gathering reaches 16 x 8 = 128 biomass a turn, so 2500/128 = ~19.5 turns of baskets; hunting Red Deer the retreat leaves ~5.6 kills a turn, so 250/5.6 = ~45 turns of spears and 5000/(5.6 x 15) = ~60 turns of sled). Closing that gap is a balance change, not a comment fix, and it belongs with the hunt-effectiveness tuning tracked on issue #495. THE QUANTA ARE INDEPENDENT BY CONSTRUCTION: a band that only hunts wears no baskets and a band that only gathers wears no sled. KNOWN SKEW, a config problem not a model one: a per-KILL charge is species-blind, so a party on Wild Fowl shreds the same spears in ~4.5 turns. The quantum is deliberate (docs/plan_denial_raid.md 1.2 requires wear to track USE, and for a spear a use IS a kill); if small game proves to wreck the pacing, the lever is a per-species use cost, not a turn clock.
_comment_kits: THE KIT ROSTER - what a party is SENT OUT WITH, chosen by name instead of implicitly using whatever the band owns. A kit is a MASK over the items above: effective_equipped(item) = kit uses it AND the band still has condition in it. `big_game` and `gathering` reproduce the pre-roster behaviour exactly, so choosing them is bit-for-bit the shipped game. `none` is an ORDINARY ROSTER MEMBER and NOT a sentinel: it simply uses nothing, so every predicate reads false and the party runs at the unequipped tiers throughout - and, because wear rides the same predicate, spends no durability on any item. That is what makes a bare-handed comparison free to run: it must not consume the very kit it is being compared against. `trapping` is the first kit that is not a subset of the old behaviour: traps clear no defence (a trapper falls back to the bare hand's attack 1), so it takes ONLY quarry with no defence at all - rabbit, fowl, grouse, snow hare, catfish - and on exactly that quarry it is the better instrument, because reach and not damage is what binds there. It carries the sled too: a trapper still has to get the catch home. `jobs` is what a kit may be sent on; a kit named for a job it does not list is a COMMAND FAILURE, never a silent fall back to the default. `default_kits` is what each verb uses when the player names none.
